thread:
sophia: heads-up — tried to apply the poetry lock update that includes the starlette CVE fix (CVE-2025-0421). CI is failing on FastAPI tests.
jonathan: ugh. which package version did poetry pick up for starlette?
sophia: it upgraded to 0.21.0 from 0.20.4. changelog shows minor API reshuffle around routing imports.
alex: fastapi still pins router imports expecting the old module layout, so runtime errors in test logs.
maya: can you paste the failing stacktrace? ci-bot: ```ERROR TypeError: Router has no attribute 'add_route'
  File "/app/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/fastapi/routing.py", line 42, in <module>
    from starlette.routing import Router
```
sophia: exact. failing in unit tests that import FastAPI internals.
jonathan: is the CVE fix only available in 0.21.0? could we apply the security patch while keeping API compatibility?
sophia: looks like the fix landed in 0.21.0. starlette maintainers moved some symbols around. No backport yet.
alex: options: (1) pin starlette<0.21.0 and delay CVE fix (2) bump fastapi to a version compatible with starlette 0.21.0 (3) patch our code/tests to adapt.
maya: fastapi upstream has a PR for starlette 0.21 compatibility but not released. Bumping fastapi now might pull other deps.
dependabot: [bot] opened PR #423: "poetry.lock: update starlette to 0.21.0 to address CVE-2025-0421"
sophia: CI shows additional failures with tokenizers wheel on mac-latest runner when we bumped transformers -> 4.40.2 in the same lock update. Separate but in same lockfile.
jonathan: great. so two regressions at once. Risk of cascading changes.
alex: propose immediate mitigation: revert bot PR, create targeted PR that pins starlette<0.21.0 and adds a follow-up issue to track fastapi/starlette upgrade. Meanwhile open security exception for hosted API until we can stage a compatible upgrade.
maya: can we instead vendor the small security change from starlette and apply it as a patch package? maybe create a tiny shim to restore old import paths.
sophia: vendor patch might be quickest. but needs audit — small surface but changes runtime imports. plus we must ensure private deployments' lockfiles don't diverge weirdly.
jonathan: what's the customer impact? is the vulnerability exploitable in our deployment modes? alex: starlette CVE is SSRF via malformed ASGI scope headers — exploitable only when untrusted clients can craft headers. Our public hosted endpoints are exposed but have reverse proxies that block suspicious headers; still we should treat high severity.
maya: ok, priority high. plan: 1) revert bot PR to unblock CI and other PRs (sophia to revert) 2) open targeted patch PR that vendors minimal fix + tests (maya to draft) 3) meanwhile coordinate with platform to add a WAF rule to mitigate header vectors for hosted for 72h (alex to ask infra) 4) track fastapi release and schedule a follow-up upgrade with integration tests (jonathan to own).
sophia: starting revert now.
ci-bot: Revert PR merged by sophia — build queued.
sophia: also adding security-note in the revert PR describing follow-ups and timeline.
jonathan: for transformers/tokenizers failure — separate PR: pin `tokenizers==0.15.3` wheel build issues on mac, we should prefer manylinux wheels or install from sdist as fallback. maya will open that.
maya: opening tokenizer pin PR and adding a CI matrix change to use linux runners for heavy wheel builds.
alex: also add a poetry constraint file (constraints.txt) so dependabot can't do broad bumps that combine multiple major changes in one lock update.
sophia: agreed. let's keep lockfile bump PRs focused — one vulnerability per PR ideally.
jonathan: I'll draft a short incident note for security channel summarizing mitigation and timeline.
sophia: thanks everyone. will follow up with PR links.
maya: :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Build passed on revert at 1781241799."
